inputs.share_count_basis: Basic shares on issue ~53.8m (H1 2026 attributable NI 430 / basic EPS 7.99; FY2025 1,016 / 18.90 = 53.76). Held FLAT. The EUR 500m 0.05% convertible (2027) is out of the money at the current price and is carried as debt (EUR 491m inside gross financial debt / net_debt), so it is not added to the count as well -- doing both would double-count it. MAP employee matching shares are immaterial (EUR 7m liability).
inputs.sbc_source: No material equity-settled SBC. The Performance Share Plan (PSP/LTI) is CASH-settled (FY2025 AR 'Share-based compensation' note, line ~13600), so its cost is already in personnel expense and OCF; Executive Board share-based grants EUR 5m (FY2025). MAP employee share programme liability EUR 14m (Dec-25) / 7m (Jun-26). No net-share-settlement taxes. SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR build: 10y Bund ~2.7%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.05 -> cost of equity ~8.5-8.8%; net debt plus pensions under 15% of EV, after-tax cost of debt ~3% -> WACC 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, GTF-programme concentration and USD exposure are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities EUR 464m (30-Jun-2026) sit inside gross financial debt and therefore inside net_debt; lease principal (financing, EUR 42m H1-26 / ~EUR 100m p.a. run-rate) is NOT deducted from the flows; ongoing lease renewal is charged via ~0.9pp of revenue inside capex_pct_path. lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI deducted once in the equity bridge (NCI share of NI ~EUR 12m p.a., FY2025 1,028 vs 1,016 attributable, capitalised at ~12.5x = EUR 150m). NCI book equity EUR 57m.
inputs.fx_note: Reporting and quote currency both EUR; no conversion. Note MTU's revenue is ~80% USD-denominated -- FY2026 guidance assumes USD 1.20/EUR, versus ~1.13 average in 2025, which mechanically depresses EUR revenue growth.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (EUR-built WACC, single lease treatment, NCI once, SBC-zero). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: MTU is an operating company (engine-module OEM partner in IAE V2500, PW1100G GTF, GEnx, GE9X, plus the commercial MRO arm and military EJ200/TP400), not a bank/REIT/holdco. No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry -- this is a fresh build. NORMALISATION: FY2023 statutory EBIT (-161) and FY2023-26 cash flow are distorted by the PW1100G powder-metal (GTF fleet management plan) charge; the forward flows are built on ADJUSTED EBIT (which strips the GTF and IAE-V2500 stake-acquisition special items) at a normalised ~70% cash conversion of adjusted NOPAT, and the remaining GTF cash burden is deducted ONCE in the equity bridge as an after-tax lump. FY2025 adjusted FCF EUR 378m was ~39% of EUR 968m adjusted NI. FY2026 guidance (H1-26 report): revenue EUR 9.2-9.7bn at USD 1.20, adjusted EBIT EUR 1,350-1,450m, FCF EUR 500-600m (50-60% of adjusted NI); the model's FY2026 base flow (~EUR 695m) is ABOVE the guided FCF by roughly the 2026 GTF compensation payments, which is why the GTF residual sits in the bridge. last_fcf = reported FCF (OCF 848 - capex 515, FY2025); MTU's own adjusted FCF was EUR 378m. Interest income NOT stripped: MTU is a net-debt company. Buybacks: none (flat count is a modelling convention, not funded by repurchases). The Q3 2026 statement (due ~late October 2026) is not yet in the extracted set; refresh guidance when it is.

equity_bridge.note: EUR 675m (644 non-current + 31 current, 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet) x (1 - 27% normalised group tax rate). Service cost is inside EBITDA; the funded deficit is debt-like.

equity_bridge.item: Residual GTF fleet-management-plan cash burden, after tax
equity_bridge.note: Estimate. Refund liabilities for warranty and liability risks EUR 410m at 30-Jun-2026 (485 at Dec-25), stated by MTU to be driven by the GTF fleet management plan, which runs into 2026; taken after the 27% tax shield (~EUR 300m). Excluded from the normalised flows, so charged here exactly once.
NCI share of profit ~EUR 12m p.a. capitalised at ~12.5x; book NCI EUR 57m.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2026 guidance midpoint (+7.8% at USD 1.20) fading to ~3%; equity 5yr CAGR (10.7%) is flattered by the post-COVID recovery and depressed by the FY2023 GTF loss, so it is not used mechanically
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 10.7% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 17.1% and EPS 5yr CAGR 48.4% -- divergence well over 30%. Both revenue and EPS start from the COVID trough (FY2020) and EPS from the GTF-hit FY2023 on the 3yr view, so neither is a forward run-rate.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is zero (cash-settled PSP), so owner FCF = reported FCF and the owner-FCF CAGRs equal the reported ones. FCF 3yr CAGR is negative (-1.4%) despite 18% revenue growth because FY2024-25 cash flow absorbed GTF compensation payments and working-capital build for the OEM ramp; that is the gap the equity-bridge GTF deduction and the -22% working-capital capture are meant to capture.

base.narrative: FY2026 at guidance midpoint (revenue ~EUR 9.45bn at USD 1.20, adjusted EBIT ~EUR 1.4bn = 14.8%); growth ~7-8% through 2029 on narrowbody production ramps and GTF/V2500 shop visits, fading to 3%. 2030 revenue ~EUR 12.4bn -- below management's EUR 13-14bn 2030 target (Paris Air Show, June 2025), roughly the FX haircut of USD 1.20 vs the ~1.10 the target was set at. Adjusted EBITDA margin 19.4% -> 20.0% (adjusted EBIT ~15.5%, the top of the 14.5-15.5% 2030 target range).
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Adjusted EBIT margin + D&A. FY2025 adjusted EBIT ~14.8% (guided FY2026 14.3-15.4% on the 9.2-9.7bn range); D&A ~4.6% (H1-26 EUR 218m).
base.capex_pct_path_note: PPE + intangibles + acquired programme assets/development (~5.7% FY2025, EUR 515m) plus ~0.9pp lease renewal under treatment (A); capacity build-out (Serbia, Zhuhai, Poland MRO shops) moderates after 2028.
base.wc_capture_pct_note: Negative: MTU's operating working capital (inventories 2,070 + receivables 1,818 + contract assets 1,479 + aftermarket compensation assets 1,108 less payables 509, contract liabilities 503 and refund liabilities 3,383) is ~22% of revenue, so growth consumes cash.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: Group normalised rate 27%, FY2025 effective 24.6%; 26% used. Cash taxes were lower in 2024-25 because GTF payments are deductible as paid; that shield travels with the GTF lump in the bridge, which is taken after tax.

bull.narrative: Top of guidance and above: A320neo/A220 rates and 787 deliveries hit plan, spare-parts list-price escalation stays high, the aged V2500 fleet keeps flying, GTF Advantage resolves durability, European defence spending lifts EJ200/TP400. 2030 revenue ~EUR 13.4bn (inside the EUR 13-14bn target despite USD 1.20) and adjusted EBITDA margin ~21% (adjusted EBIT ~16.5%, above the target range).

bear.narrative: Air-traffic shock (oil above USD 95, Middle East conflict, recession) plus a weaker USD: spare-parts demand stalls, airframers miss rate targets, and the PW1100G needs further inspection/compensation rounds beyond the 2026 end-date, compressing OEM margins; GTF-heavy MRO mix (40-45% of MRO revenue) dilutes margins and the post-GTF shop-visit wave fades. Adjusted EBITDA margin slips to 18% (adj EBIT ~13.5%).

scenario_narratives.base: MTU executes its FY2026 guidance (revenue EUR 9.2-9.7bn, adjusted EBIT EUR 1.35-1.45bn) and grows high single digits through 2029 on narrowbody production ramps, record installed-base shop visits on V2500 and GTF, and military growth; margins drift up ~1pp as spare-parts pricing holds. Cash conversion normalises to ~70% of adjusted NOPAT once the GTF fleet management plan payments end (charged once in the bridge), with working capital still absorbing ~22c per euro of incremental revenue.
scenario_narratives.bull: The aftermarket super-cycle runs longer: aircraft scarcity keeps old V2500s and CFM-era fleets flying, spare-parts list prices escalate faster than costs, GTF durability fixes cut shop-visit costs, and European rearmament lifts the military segment. Revenue compounds ~8% for a decade with adjusted EBIT margins reaching ~17%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cycle turns: an oil/geopolitical shock hits air traffic and spare-parts demand just as further PW1100G findings extend compensation and inspection costs past 2026; a USD at 1.25+ erodes EUR revenue and margins (partially hedged), and the GTF-heavy MRO mix keeps margins near 13.5% adjusted EBIT. Growth slows to 2-5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: MTU's earnings rest heavily on one programme family (PW1100G/GTF) whose powder-metal remediation is still being finalised in 2026 and whose estimates come from RTX/P&W rather than MTU, and the aftermarket is cyclical and USD-exposed. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things at once (aftermarket pricing, airframer ramp execution, GTF durability fix, defence uplift). Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Normalised owner-FCF DCF on adjusted EBIT, with the one-off GTF cash burden, pensions and NCI taken explicitly in the equity bridge. SBC is immaterial (cash-settled PSP already in OCF), so house and street bases coincide.
key_risks_to_valuation: PW1100G/GTF: further inspection findings or compensation beyond the 2026 end-date would enlarge the EUR 300m bridge deduction and depress OEM margins.
USD/EUR: ~80% of revenue is USD; guidance assumes 1.20. A 10% USD move swings EUR revenue and, partly hedged, EBIT.
Aftermarket cyclicality: spare-parts pricing and shop-visit volumes are the profit engine; an air-traffic shock hits them first.

Working-capital intensity: the -22% capture on incremental revenue is the largest single cash driver; if the OEM ramp needs more inventory and contract assets, conversion stays near the guided 50-60%.
Terminal value is ~70%+ of EV on a 10-year horizon; the cap multiples (15/18/20x) bound it.
